questions.question: What is a lambda in Java?
options: An anonymous function that can be passed as a value
A class with a single method
A static variable
A type of loop
explanations: Correct. A lambda is an anonymous function that can be passed as an argument or assigned to a variable.
That describes a functional interface, not the lambda itself.
A lambda is not a static variable.
A lambda is not a loop.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax of a lambda?
options: (parameters) -> { body }
(parameters) => { body }
lambda(parameters) { body }
function(parameters) { body }
explanations: Correct. The lambda syntax uses an arrow (->) between parameters and body.
=> is JavaScript/TypeScript syntax, not Java.
lambda is not a keyword in Java.
function is not the lambda syntax in Java.

questions.question: What is a functional interface?
options: An interface with a single abstract method
An interface with multiple methods
An abstract class
A static method
explanations: Correct. A functional interface has exactly one abstract method, which allows using lambdas with it.
An interface with multiple methods is not functional.
It is not an abstract class; it is an interface.
A static method does not define a functional interface.

questions.question: What is Predicate<T>?
options: A function that takes T and returns boolean
A function that takes T and returns R
A function that takes nothing and returns T
A function that takes two Ts and returns boolean
explanations: Correct. Predicate<T> evaluates a condition: it takes a T and returns a boolean.
That is Function<T,R>.
That is Supplier<T>.
That would be a BiPredicate<T,T>.

questions.question: What is Function<T,R>?
options: A function that takes T and returns R
A function that takes T and returns boolean
A function that takes nothing
A function that takes R and returns T
explanations: Correct. Function<T,R> transforms a value of type T into a value of type R.
That is Predicate<T>.
That is Supplier<T>.
That would be Function<R,T>.
